facts.P1_fx_receipts: Yes, into a domiciliary (USD) account; no prior approval needed.
facts.P2_fcy_account: Yes: a domiciliary account at a Nigerian bank.
facts.P3_local_gateways: Paystack lets you sign up as a Starter Business without CAC registration.
facts.L1_registration: Not needed under your own name; register a business name with CAC.
facts.L2_tax_id: Every taxable person needs a Tax ID, and banks will ask for it.
facts.L3_income_tax_foreign: Foreign income is taxable; the first ₦800,000 is tax-free, then 15–25%.
facts.L4_vat_gst: VAT is 7.5%; exported services are zero-rated.
facts.L5_data_protection: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, enforced by the NDPC.
facts.L6_consumer_ecommerce: Consumer law (FCCPA) covers online sellers; complaints go to the FCCPC.
facts.L7_incentives: First ₦800,000 of income is tax-free; small companies pay 0% company tax.
facts.D1_id_document: National Identification Number (NIN); payment apps also use your BVN.

watch_out.text: Paystack Starter accounts are capped at ₦8 million (USD 5,000 for dollars).
Platforms that pay through PayPal Payouts can't pay Nigerian accounts.
All your foreign income is taxable, even if you keep it abroad.
